description:
The Abyssal War

v0.6.1 - the hive arms once it can pay - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Download

AbyssalWar-0.6.1.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. It extracts to mods/ThreatIncursion - overwrite your existing folder rather than keeping both. Saves made with Threat Incursion carry over: the mod id has not changed.

Core concept

At game start a new system in the outer reaches of the sector will be seeded with several Threat colonies. Once these colonies develop they will spread to neighbouring systems in the search for resources to fund new colonies, which is what they need to expand the hive. As they get within a certain distance of the core worlds, they will start sending out first-strike parties and attempt to siege any planet within range. Human factions will mobilise when attacked and enter a war economy, leading to counter attacks and strikes of their own.

Instant War - Fast start for existing save

If you are midway through a playthrough you can temporarily enable the Instant War setting, load your save, wait for the system to populate then save and exit and disable instant war. You can also change how many systems are instantly colonised and their general size and strength.

The Threat: every system you have found, in priority order - vitality, swarms, reach, strikes out, and what each one makes.

Any mobilised faction, read the same way: the Persean League's reserves, its two fronts on Gamma Brador, and the aid you can send.

Player mobilisation

There is a lot of pressure for the player to get setup with colonies quickly in this game mode. If this is not your jam you can change when the Threat spawn, to be after the Abyssal questline finishes, or when your first colony reaches size 6. Once you have your own colonies you can mobilise to enter the war yourself. You will have a set amount of resources available depending on your colony industries, size and military structures. You will have complete control over your fleets and supplies and where to direct your war engine.

Your own war: colony reserves and convoys, your own front pushing on the hive world Gamma Hero I, and the fleets supplying and defending it.

Sieges

It is important to note while you can override marine actions they will function autonomously and react to various events like counter attacks and bombardments themselves. I'm listing the various interactions below but dont stress and think you have to manage them all. Ultimately if you want a siege to properly succeed make sure your control the space above the planet and it should be enough for the marines to get the job done. If they need resupply it will be automatically sent from the nearest colony assuming it has spare resources and FP. Otherwise you can always resupply them yourself. Keep in mind the Threat will send defensive swarms from neighbouring systems to take back control and if left alone will start bombing your marines from orbit.

Whichever faction controls the orbit affects the ground battle below, in the form of direct fire support.A contested orbit blocks bombardment, landings, supply convoys and withdrawals, so it is always the first fight.As the siege progresses military structures on the planet are disrupted proportional to the strength of the attackers, and their bonuses reduce proportional to disruption duration.Fortifications shoot back. A fleet parked in orbit bleeds hulls to the batteries, faster the better defended the world.Orbit alone can only take a world so far - there is a floor it cannot grind past. Getting past it needs boots on the ground.Troops land either once the defences are suppressed as far as orbit can take them, or immediately if the force is already large enough to hold the ground. Ships or marines - your choice which you spend.A front can dig in or push. Digging in builds entrenchment over time and keeps casualties low. Pushing takes ground a layer at a time - strata on a hive, districts on a colony - but at heavy losses and no cover.Fronts burn armaments. A dry front bleeds badly and fights at half strength. The Threat is the exception: its fronts need no supply, but pay double casualties whenever they assault.The defender counter-attacks periodically, faster the more it outnumbers the front. Losing one costs troops and hands a layer back; a front holding no ground can be wiped outright.Marines gain veterancy through the campaign, fighting harder and dying less, and carry that experience back to your fleet when they withdraw.Take a hive and it is destroyed, you get a free outpost on the ruin stocked with whatever your troops had left, and the Threat holds a grudge over it.Lose a colony to the Threat and it decivilises, with a new hive seeded on the wreckage.Fleets can be sent to Support a front, which bombards regardless, or Defend it, which only fires when the front actually needs it and never while your own troops are assaulting.Tactical bombardment counts as a short siege run. With your own troops on the ground you can call it in danger close - it costs you marines, but reaches organs orbit cannot otherwise touch.Everything moves by real convoy. Supply runs, reinforcements and relief are fleets that can be intercepted and looted.

For Starsector 0.98a-RC8. Vanilla-only, LunaLib optional, incompatible with Nex. Safe to add mid-save; removing it mid-war breaks the save. Every number is configurable via LunaLib (Shift+F2) or data/config/settings.json.

Spoiler

Fix: the hive never grew past size 3.

Every hive world built its Ground Defenses at size 3, and those batteries demand metals the hive could not yet make - a size-3 world has one industry slot and Mining holds it. The unmet demand held vitality on the stall floor, so no world reached size 4, no refinery was ever built, and the whole war stayed dormant (Reach and Strikes dashed, Swarms idle). Present since 0.4.0; every save started on 0.6.0 is affected.

The hive now builds Ground Defenses and Heavy Batteries only when it can feed them - the machinery and metals they demand at least half-met, the same bar a growth input must clear. A bare mining world grows to 4, builds its refinery, and arms on the next tick.Existing saves heal on load. A frozen hive - no refinery anywhere, size-3 worlds with batteries on the stall floor and no free slot - gets each such world the one size the freeze cost it and its production chain stood up in the same load. [close]0.6.0 - the war layer
SpoilerThreat Incursion is now The Abyssal War. The mod id is unchanged, so existing saves keep working.

Ground war
  • Eradication is a ground campaign, not a decline timer: land marines, take the strata, kill the Fabrication Core.
  • Ground fronts push, dig in or withdraw; armaments burn per marine per day, so what a front carries is how long it lasts.
  • Fronts push the moment troops land at holding strength; a dug-in front stays dug in until the next landing.
  • Sieges fight for the orbit first. Bombardment wears fortification to a floor and no further - a front on the ground takes it the rest of the way.
  • Threat strikes land fronts of their own on inhabited worlds, dig in, then make a final push.
  • Colony defense is garrison troops times fortification, each worn down separately, with an orbital floor under the structures.
  • Marines arm over weeks, take casualties, count toward counter-attacks, and carry veterancy both ways with your fleet's marine pool.
  • Support and Defend fleet orders: hold the orbit, run the siege slice, or fight only while the front cannot hold.
  • A Defend fleet at the orbital floor can break up its own hulls into troops for the front.
  • Planetary shields buy real cover against orbital bombardment.
  • The hive scours an unopposed enemy front after three days.

Strategy layer
  • NPC factions enter war mode when the Threat strikes them; you mobilise or stand down yourself.
  • Every colony banks a visible reserve of marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies.
  • Convoys carry that stock physically - escort them, or let the swarm's raiders have them.
  • Fleet orders from the board: guard, stage, intercept, support, defend, siege, recall.
  • Guarding your own colony stages the fleet there: its strength counts at the host and folds into sorties.
  • Faction view shows any mobilised faction's colonies, reserves and fleets, with a totals row and a colour key.
  • Min / Med / Max load ladders on sieges, supply runs and convoy loads.
  • Recalled and expired fleets sail home and return their surviving cargo.
  • Sieges are leashed to the contested orbit; strays are recalled instead of chasing across the sector.

Player aid and outposts
  • NPC factions are autonomous now: you aid them, you do not command them.
  • Send Defend, Resupply, Reinforce or Strike from your own colonies, gated by a capacity ledger and reserve stock, earning standing on arrival.
  • Factions post their needs as ordinary missions - deliver by colony fleet, or in person at the dock.
  • Allies send each other aid by standing, without you.
  • Build an outpost over any uncolonised world, or take one free by ground victory. Dock at it for storage, or decommission it.
  • A later colony on that world inherits the outpost.

Economy
  • War reserves are the colony's real resource stockpile, not a separate hidden ledger.
  • Mobilised colonies carry the War Footing condition, so the war shows as genuine demand and a real shortage on the colony screen.
  • Depots cover the colony's own shortages before they fund anything else.
  • Convoys land as trade at the receiving colony.
  • Bases need a Waystation; NPC mobilisation builds them.

Escalation
  • Grudge and alarm: the swarm answers whoever hurts it most, and alarm speeds hive fabrication.
  • A ground victory draws retaliation from the nearest hive.
  • Coalition fleets answer a mobilised faction's call during a siege.
  • Defense Swarms detach to raid convoys, then return to their garrison.

Board
  • Ground Fronts table, per system, with order buttons on every front.
  • Per-fleet rows with Recall and Intercept.
  • Colony rows open vanilla's own colony screen.
  • Purge commissions removed; sieges launch from the faction view.
  • Tooltips rewritten: one line per fact, and every button says what pressing it does - or why it cannot be pressed.
  • The intel list row reads at vanilla's own size now, next to Colony Crises.

Testing

It implements complex siege mechanics involving orbital control, ground troop movements, and supply lines. Players can mobilize their own colonies, manage fleets, and interact with AI factions who autonomously wage war.
